Private_Sector_Practice: Public quarterly SOE performance dashboard with standardised KPIs
Origin_Domain: Listed-company quarterly reporting + investor KPI disclosure
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: Publicly listed firms report results on a fixed quarterly calendar against a standard metric set; visibility itself disciplines management and lets owners act.
Axis1_Justification: Directly operationalises OECD II.F.4, V.A.1 and V.E - a monitoring obligation with no teeth becomes visible when published.
Axis2_Justification: Costs little: publish what the SOE already reports internally. Feasible even with a small central unit, though standardising 20+ SOEs takes time.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Define a minimum common KPI set (8-12 metrics) before publishing; stagger by portfolio size.

Private_Sector_Practice: Board performance evaluation leading to a mandatory remedial action plan
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: Boards in listed companies are evaluated annually; the review produces a scored action plan that is tracked. Non-improvement is visible and career-relevant.
Axis1_Justification: Verbatim OECD 'good practice' in Annotations to VI.I - the benchmark itself recommends it.
Axis2_Justification: Uses existing directors and a light external facilitator. No new statutory body needed. Main cost is C1: finding an evaluator who is not socially entangled with the board.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Use a regional (CARICOM or UWI) evaluator pool rather than a local one, to weaken C2 and C1 at the same time.

Private_Sector_Practice: Balanced Scorecard cascade from owner mandate to unit level
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: Translates strategy into a small set of financial and non-financial measures across four perspectives, then cascades to business units and individuals.
Axis1_Justification: Converts vague SOE mandates into measurable objectives; supports OECD II.F.3 and sharpens the distinction between commercial and policy objectives.
Axis2_Justification: A designed process, not a capital project. The binding limit is C4: where no comparator exists, measures must be absolute trends not league tables.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Use self-referential benchmarks (year-on-year, per-unit-cost, service reliability) instead of cross-firm comparison, because C4 removes true comparators.
Evidence_Source_In_Corpus: OECD II.F.3; Annotations to Ch. II on benchmarking

Private_Sector_Practice: Integrated reporting linking strategy to outcomes
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: An integrated report shows how strategy, governance, performance and prospects create value, and states explicitly where the company fell short and what it will do about it.
Axis1_Justification: Mirrors OECD V.A.1 (objectives and their fulfilment) and the Ch. VII expectation to disclose corrective action for underperformance.
Axis2_Justification: Adds discipline to reports SOEs already produce; does not require new legislation.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Start with an 'objectives and fulfilment' table in the existing annual report rather than adopting a full integrated-reporting framework.

Private_Sector_Practice: Remedial / special-measures regime: publishable recovery plan with a named accountable executive
Origin_Domain: Listed-company restructuring plans / turnaround and administration processes
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: When a listed company underperforms, a named executive owns a dated recovery plan; failure to show progress escalates to closure, sale or removal.
Axis1_Justification: This is the strongest available substitute for the takeover/bankruptcy disciplines the OECD itself says SOEs are insulated from.
Axis2_Justification: C6 is the killing constraint: governments cannot credibly threaten to let an essential service fail. C2 makes naming and removing a person socially expensive.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Soften the terminal sanction (closure) into a graduated ladder: board replacement, then CEO removal, then external management contract, then divestment.
Evidence_Source_In_Corpus: OECD Ch. I/II annotation on takeover and bankruptcy being unavailable to SOEs; VI.B

Private_Sector_Practice: Hard budget constraint with performance-contract tranching
Origin_Domain: Contractual performance management in the private sector + earned-autonomy regimes
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: Funding is released in tranches against verified milestones; no milestone means no money. Removes automatic recapitalisation.
Axis1_Justification: Attacks the soft-budget constraint directly, which is the mechanism C6 names in your manual.
Axis2_Justification: Governments have repeatedly recapitalised essential SOEs with no conditions. A statutory no-bailout rule is easy to write and near-impossible to enforce in a crisis.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Tranche only the discretionary investment/expansion envelope; accept that the standing wage bill must be met, and make the tranche review public.
Evidence_Source_In_Corpus: OECD II.F.3; III.C on public service obligation funding

Private_Sector_Practice: Independent audit committee with an audit-report deadline and automatic parliamentary escalation
Origin_Domain: Audit committee best practice and statutory reporting deadlines
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: Companies face hard filing deadlines and an independent committee. Escalation converts silence into a reportable event.
Axis1_Justification: Directly creates a consequence for non-disclosure, filling the gap left by OECD V.D which mandates audit but attaches no timeliness sanction.
Axis2_Justification: Statutory drafting is cheap, and the region has existing audit capacity. The risk is creating another report nobody reads (see the PAC-backlog literature).
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Attach the escalation to an existing body (the PAC or a standing finance committee) rather than creating a new oversight unit, to avoid C3 duplicate fixed costs.

Private_Sector_Practice: Executive performance-related pay with malus and clawback
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: Pay is weighted to measures, and a malus/clawback clause lets the company withhold or recover pay already granted if results were misstated.
Axis1_Justification: Explicitly named as 'good practice' in the Annotations to Ch. VI.
Axis2_Justification: Pay levels in Caribbean SOEs are politically visible and compressed; increasing them, let alone withholding them, is a public controversy. C6 also caps the pool.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Apply malus/clawback as a reputational and pensionable-service consequence rather than a cash one, since the cash pool is too small to deter.
Evidence_Source_In_Corpus: OECD Annotations to Ch. VI on malus and clawback

Private_Sector_Practice: Named-accountability operational reporting with mandatory exception explanation and block-on-send
Origin_Domain: Front-line operations management / aviation ground-handling shift control
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: Every exception on a shift must carry a written reason, a named owner and the action taken. The report cannot be transmitted until mandatory fields are complete, so silence is structurally impossible.
Axis1_Justification: An SOE-native working example: it operationalises OECD V.A.1, II.F.4 and the integrity expectation that breaches meet consequences, and it manufactures the C2-free accountability that policy documents lack.
Axis2_Justification: Already built and in use inside a Bahamian SOE. Requires no legislation, no new budget line, and no independent cohort - it works precisely because the escalations are defined in advance.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Extend upward: apply the same mandatory-exception discipline to the monthly SOE-to-ownership-entity return, so the block-on-send rule reaches the board and the Ministry of Finance.

Private_Sector_Practice: Whistleblowing channel with protection and a duty to act
What_It_Is_And_Why_It_Works_Privately: An independent channel lets staff report misconduct safely; the company must act and report on outcomes.
Axis1_Justification: Supports OECD Ch. V integrity and Annotations, but the evidence base on effectiveness in small states is weak and it is not primarily a performance-consequence mechanism.
Axis2_Justification: Channels exist in several jurisdictions already. The obstacle is C2 - anonymity is fragile where everyone knows everyone.
Adaptation_Needed_For_SIDS: Route the channel to a regional or external body rather than a local one, otherwise the reporting party is identifiable by default.
